title: Local events are missing from the collector
scenario: R1’s memory buffer includes the representative link, OSPF and configuration records below. The collector received the two level-3 LINK events but not the displayed level-5 events. Its configuration was unchanged during the interval. The team requires remote records at levels 0–6. Interpret the router’s threshold rather than assuming ping or a logging-host status guarantees delivery.

question: Which displayed setting explains why these level-5 events are ineligible for the remote destination?
options: The remote threshold excludes the level-5 records before forwarding.
The local buffer threshold prevents the router from generating level-5 events.
The monitor setting replaces the remote threshold for an active SSH session.
The collector destination requires replaying old buffered events before accepting new ones.
explanation: The errors threshold permits levels 0–3, excluding the displayed level-5 records before remote forwarding. Console and buffer settings are independent. The received level-3 records establish those particular deliveries, not that every datagram or future event must arrive.
fix:
Change the remote threshold to match the stated requirement.

```ios
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# logging trap informational
R1(config)# end
R1# show logging
```

Generate a harmless new configuration event in the isolated lab and verify the corresponding record on the collector. The new threshold makes levels 0–6 eligible; it does not replay the old buffer or guarantee transport/retention. Save after verification.

title: A downstream router will not synchronize
scenario: R2 is configured to use R1 at 10.0.12.1. Both routers now report unsynchronized status. The team has an approved alternate time source at 203.0.113.20: R1’s correctly placed capture confirms successful NTP exchanges with that alternate, and it advertises synchronized stratum 2. R1 currently has only the old source 203.0.113.10 configured. These representative excerpts establish source state; they do not establish the cause of the old source’s failure.

exhibits.title: R2# show ntp status
exhibits.text:
Clock is unsynchronized, stratum 16, no reference clock
nominal freq is 250.0000 Hz, actual freq is 250.0000 Hz, precision is 2**10
...
system poll interval is 64, never updated.

exhibits.title: R1# show ntp status
exhibits.text:
Clock is unsynchronized, stratum 16, no reference clock
nominal freq is 250.0000 Hz, actual freq is 250.0000 Hz, precision is 2**10
...
system poll interval is 64, last update was 61240 sec ago.

exhibits.title: R1# ping 203.0.113.10
exhibits.text:
Type escape sequence to abort.
Sending 5, 100-byte ICMP Echos to 203.0.113.10, timeout is 2 seconds:
.....
Success rate is 0 percent (0/5)

question: Which displayed condition prevents R1 from supplying usable synchronized time to R2?
options: R2 must become a local master before accepting time from R1
R1 is currently unsynchronized and cannot provide a usable synchronized source to R2
R2 must use a symmetric peer association solely because R1 is a router
The failed ICMP test proves every NTP datagram is blocked by a WAN ACL
explanation: R1’s own stratum-16 status shows that it is not a usable synchronized source at this time. The old-source ping failure does not identify a specific route or filtering cause. Correct R1’s intended source, then separately verify R2’s association and local state.
fix:
Use the approved alternate source with the successful NTP evidence stated in the scenario.

```ios
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# no ntp server 203.0.113.10
R1(config)# ntp server 203.0.113.20
R1(config)# end
R1# show ntp associations
R1# show ntp status
```

Wait for actual source selection. R1 should then report stratum 3; R2, if it successfully synchronizes to R1, reports stratum 4. Inspect R2’s associations/status and clock as well. Do not declare R1’s unsourced clock authoritative with ntp master merely to remove an alarm. Investigate the old source separately and save the verified approved configuration.
